## 10. Optical NTT engine in the full system (ark set, baseline algorithm)

| design | bootstrap | mJ | conversions | optical busy | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small digital, no optics | 17.46 ms | 1280 | 0 | 0% | NTT-bound |
| + realistic engine (block 16, ENOB 12) | 401.38 ms | 46861 | 2.68e+11 | 89% | NTT-bound (optical engine) |
| + realistic engine, ENOB 16, 36-bit limbs* | 620.39 ms | 89183 | 4.67e+10 | 98% | NTT-bound (optical engine) |
| + ideal engine (exact at any precision, block 4096) | 12.59 ms | 1375 | 3.59e+09 | 29% | MAC-bound |
| + ideal engine, 4x converter rate | 11.63 ms | 1318 | 3.59e+09 | 8% | MAC-bound |
| ARK-class (memory-bound), no optics | 13.94 ms | 1139 | 0 | 0% | memory-bound |
| ARK-class + ideal engine | 16.87 ms | 1632 | 3.59e+09 | 21% | memory-bound |

*36-bit limbs (SHARP's word size) with the same level structure: illustrative only. At ENOB 16 a conversion costs ~2 nJ (Walden), so the converter rate is cut to 5e10 samples/s to fit the 300 W TDP; at 5e11 the converters alone would need ~1 kW.

**Break-even converter energy for the ideal engine (energy per bootstrap equal to the small digital design)**

| laser + tuning static | break-even Walden FoM (DAC = ADC, ENOB 8) | = energy per conversion |
|---|---|---|
| 20 W | never | - |
| 5 W | 117.0 fJ/step | 30.0 pJ/sample |
| 0 W | 185.4 fJ/step | 47.5 pJ/sample |

Energy question only: the TDP is not enforced in this search, so the clock stays at 100%.
